title: Don't make my mistake
text:
Don't make my mistake. This is a revision of the review I wrote many months ago, when I first purchased this coffeemaker. I gave it three stars initially. Now that I have worked with it for months, I can report that I absolutely hate it.

The only good thing about this coffee maker is the high-quality carafe, and even that is difficult to wash without introducing water between the steel layers. I hear it sloshing around in there now I wonder what it's growing. There's no way to get it out.

The coffee maker itself is, in my experience, terrible.

Major problems:

If the carafe is even SLIGHTLY off kilter under the filter, your counter will flood. This happens again and again even though I am now neurotically careful.

Forget about making a full pot of coffee. I use standard Starbucks ground coffee, and if I try to fill the filter even three quarters of the way high, inevitably the water somehow leaves the filter compartment and gets into the water compartment, leaving my coffee full of grounds. In practice, I can only really make two thirds of a pot, never a pot up to the fill line, without ground coffee contamination of the liquid.

The plastic casing of the unit is lightweight and cheap. This didn't bother me so much until I realized how limited the overall functionality was.

This Japanese company traditionally specialized in steel carafes and later got into the coffee maker business. It shows. The coffee maker itself was a waste of money from my perspective. Back to the drawing board.

product_metadata.title: Zojirushi EC-BD15 Fresh Brew Thermal Carafe Coffee Maker
features: Stylish automatic coffee brewer with 1.5-liter thermal carafe
Stainless-steel carafe keeps coffee hot for hours
1025 watts; electronic clock/timer with preset function; auto shut-off for safety
Clever brew-and-serve lid design; easy-to-read water gauge
description: Zojirushi's EC-BD15BA 1.5 Liter Fresh Brew Coffee Maker with Vacuum Stainless Steel Carafe is gorgeous and functional and will look spectacular on your countertop. It has many wonderful features.

Lots of folks dislike the burnt flavor that coffee gets when it sits in a glass pot over a heating element. To avoid this, coffee shops often brew right into large thermal pots to keep the coffee warm without it becoming overcooked. The Zojirushi Fresh Brew does that, too, but in home-sized batches. It looks great, too, with a glossy black body and stainless steel carafe and brew basket.

To brew, lift the lid and swing the water outlet spout to one side while the filter is being loaded; the spout will return to its proper position when the lid is closed. A small red ball in the water gauge makes it extra simple to read. And an electronic clock module also serves as a timer that will start the brewer at a specified time. The carafe's lid is designed to be on during brewing, with a small cap to help keep the heat in after it's ready. The Fresh Brew also has a pause-and-serve function that stops the flow for 30 seconds while a cup of coffee is served.

To clean the brewer unit, use a solution of white vinegar and water, following the instructions in the accompanying booklet. The unit is not immersible. The exterior can be wiped with a damp soft rag; do not use abrasives or scouring pads. The filter reservoir is removable; clean with warm soapy water and rinse thoroughly. The coffee brewer measures 15 by 12 by 9 inches (includes carafe handle when unit is completely assembled), and it uses #4 cone-shaped disposable paper filters. The Fresh Brew comes with a detailed instruction booklet. Zojirushi guarantees its products with a one-year limited warranty.
